stays.name: Ivory Cave House Oia — Plunge Pool on the Caldera

host.name: Eleni
host.presence: Born in Oia; my family carved this hyposkafo cave house into the caldera rock in the 1880s. I greet every guest with chilled Assyrtiko.

highlights.title: Top 5% of homes
highlights.detail: This home is highly ranked based on ratings, reviews, and reliability.

highlights.title: Private plunge pool on the caldera
highlights.detail: One of the few cave houses on this walkway with its own heated plunge pool.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the keypad.

stays.description: A traditional hyposkafo cave house carved into Oia's caldera cliff, whitewashed inside and out with barrel-vaulted ceilings that stay cool all summer. The private terrace steps down to a heated plunge pool hanging 250 meters above the Aegean, facing the sunset the town is famous for. Renovated in 2024 with handmade cement floors, built-in sofas, and a second bedroom in the old wine cellar.
amenities: Private plunge pool - heated, open May to October

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Amelia
reviews.text: The photos genuinely undersell it. You open the terrace doors and the entire caldera is just there. We watched the sunset from the plunge pool every single evening with wine Eleni left for us. The cave bedroom is silent and cool even in the afternoon heat.

reviews.author: Rasmus
reviews.text: Be ready for the steps down from the marble walkway — but that's Oia, and it keeps the crowds off your terrace. Immaculate housekeeping, strong AC, and the best location we've had anywhere in Greece.

reviews.author: Sofia
reviews.text: Eleni met us at Ammoudi steps, carried our bags herself, and booked us a table at a taverna we'd never have found. The house is a piece of Oia history and it shows.

reviews.author: Daniel
reviews.text: Honeymoon stay. Private, romantic, spotless. The plunge pool at 7pm with the sun dropping behind Thirassia is something we'll never forget.

images.alt: Whitewashed cave house terraces and pool lit up at night
Infinity plunge pool overlooking the caldera and white buildings
Minimal white vaulted interior washed in soft daylight
View over white rooftops and the sea through an open window
Whitewashed steps in Oia leading down toward the Aegean

stays.name: Skaros View Suite — Imerovigli Infinity Pool
stays.typeLabel: Entire rental unit in Imerovigli, Greece

host.name: Nikos & Marina
host.presence: We run four suites on the Imerovigli rim and live five minutes away; breakfast baskets are delivered to your terrace each morning.

highlights.title: Top 5% of homes
highlights.detail: This home is highly ranked based on ratings, reviews, and reliability.

highlights.title: Front-row view of Skaros Rock
highlights.detail: The infinity pool and terrace look straight onto the caldera's most dramatic headland.

highlights.title: Breakfast included
highlights.detail: A Greek breakfast basket is brought to your terrace daily.

stays.description: A couples' suite dug into the rim at Imerovigli, the quietest and highest stretch of the caldera. The heated infinity pool spills toward Skaros Rock, and the bedroom's arched glass front frames the sea from the pillow. Imerovigli sits on the Fira–Oia footpath, so you can walk to dinner in Firostefani in fifteen minutes and never touch a road.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before July 20. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Chloe
reviews.text: Imerovigli over Oia, every time. Same view, none of the crowds. We floated in the pool watching Skaros change color and had the walkway nearly to ourselves at sunrise. Marina's breakfasts were enormous.

reviews.author: Hugo
reviews.text: The suite is small but perfectly designed — everything you touch feels expensive. Nikos arranged our transfer, dinner bookings, and a catamaran day without us lifting a finger.

reviews.author: Isabelle
reviews.text: The photo of the pool with Skaros behind it is real, that is exactly what you get. Quietest place we've stayed on the islands.

images.alt: White cliffside buildings above a calm sea in Imerovigli
Guest relaxing in an infinity pool with an open sea view
White terrace with chairs overlooking the Aegean
Neutral-toned bedroom with crisp white linens
Shaded terrace table and chairs facing the caldera

stays.name: The Windmill of Oia — Restored 19th-Century Landmark

host.name: Stavros
host.presence: I spent three years restoring the windmill with local stonemasons; I'll happily walk you through its history over coffee.

highlights.title: Sleep inside a real windmill
highlights.detail: A restored 19th-century flour mill on Oia's western tip — one of a handful you can stay in.

highlights.title: 360° sunset views
highlights.detail: The circular top-floor bedroom looks over the caldera, the open Aegean, and the village.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the lockbox.

stays.description: One of the last windmills standing on Oia's western point, rebuilt beam by beam with its original stone walls, timber cap, and a spiral stair connecting three round floors. The top-floor bedroom has windows on every side; the sunset crowds gather below at the castle, but from your private terrace the view is all yours. A second bedroom and bath sit in the mill keeper's cottage beside the pool deck.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before July 25. Cancel before August 10 for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Priya
reviews.text: We've stayed in Santorini four times and nothing compares to waking up in the round room with sea on every side. The restoration is museum-quality — Stavros kept the old grinding stone as the coffee table.

reviews.author: Ethan
reviews.text: The most memorable place we've ever booked. The spiral stairs are steep and the top room is snug, which is exactly what you sign up for in a real windmill. Sunset from the terrace beats the castle crowds by a mile.

reviews.author: Camille
reviews.text: Extraordinary building and location. Wind can whistle around the cap on rough nights — bring earplugs if you're a light sleeper. We'd still return tomorrow.

reviews.author: Leo
reviews.text: Felt like sleeping inside a lighthouse. Immaculate, quiet, and the keeper's cottage was perfect for our teenagers.

images.alt: Oia's windmill and white houses glowing at dusk
View over Oia rooftops to the caldera with boats below
Calm bedroom with upholstered headboard and white bedding
Bright white sitting room with natural textures
Whitewashed lane with a blue gate and flowering wall

stays.name: Fira Old Town Townhouse — 2 Min from the Cable Car

host.name: Dimitris
host.presence: Our family has lived on this lane for four generations — knock on the shop door any time you need anything.

highlights.title: In the heart of Fira
highlights.detail: Two minutes from the cable car, the caldera walkway, and the bus station to everywhere on the island.

highlights.title: Roof terrace over the old town
highlights.detail: Evening drinks with cathedral and caldera views at a fraction of cliff-house prices.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the keypad.

stays.description: A practical, comfortable townhouse on a quiet pedestrian lane in Fira's old town — the smart base if you want the whole island within reach. Buses to Oia, Akrotiri, and the beaches leave from three blocks away, the caldera path starts around the corner, and the roof terrace catches the same sunset the cliff bars charge for. Two proper bedrooms plus a sofa bed, and a kitchen stocked by the family minimarket downstairs.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Martina
reviews.text: Perfect base — we did Oia, the boat day, Akrotiri, and Perissa all by bus from around the corner. Dimitris brought us fresh bread from the shop every morning without being asked.

reviews.author: Jake
reviews.text: You're paying a third of caldera prices and giving up almost nothing. Roof terrace at sunset with beers from the minimarket was our favorite ritual.

reviews.author: Anaïs
reviews.text: Great location and spotless. Some evening noise drifts up from the bars on weekends — it's the middle of Fira, so expected.

reviews.author: Tomás
reviews.text: Ideal with children: real kitchen, two bedrooms, and gyros downstairs. The cable car to the old port is two minutes' walk.

images.alt: Fira's cliffside houses lit up at night above the caldera
White village houses stacked along the cliff edge
Open-plan living room and kitchen in neutral tones
Warmly lit bedroom with dark timber details
Modern bathroom with a glass walk-in shower

stays.name: Blue Shutters of Firostefani — Caldera Balcony Apartment
stays.typeLabel: Entire rental unit in Firostefani, Greece

host.name: Katerina
host.presence: I live in the house behind the courtyard — you'll smell my orange cake on Sunday mornings and there's always a slice for guests.

highlights.title: Caldera view without the climb
highlights.detail: Firostefani's walkway is flat between Fira and Imerovigli — rare on the rim.

highlights.title: Bougainvillea courtyard
highlights.detail: A shaded private courtyard off the famous blue-domed church square.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the lockbox.

stays.description: A classic island apartment with sky-blue shutters, a vine-shaded courtyard, and a balcony that looks over Firostefani's blue-domed church to the caldera beyond. Firostefani is Fira's quieter sister — ten minutes' flat walk to town, steps from the most photographed dome on the island, and home to tavernas that still fill with locals in the evening.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before July 18. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Nora
reviews.text: The famous blue dome is literally around the corner — we had coffee on the balcony watching photographers queue for the shot we got from bed. Katerina's orange cake is real and it is wonderful.

reviews.author: Ben
reviews.text: Quiet, pretty, and the flat walk into Fira makes such a difference after a day out. Great value for a real caldera view.

reviews.author: Giulia
reviews.text: The courtyard smells of jasmine at night. Small kitchen but we only ever used it for breakfast — too many good tavernas nearby.

images.alt: Caldera cove with moored yachts seen from a cliff terrace
Blue-domed churches above the caldera on a clear day
Sun loungers beside a pool draped in bougainvillea
Airy white bedroom with minimal decor
White bathroom with checkerboard tile floor

stays.name: Kamares House — Traditional Home in Pyrgos Village
stays.typeLabel: Entire home in Pyrgos Kallistis, Greece

host.name: Yiannis
host.work: Vine grower for a Pyrgos winery
host.presence: I tend Assyrtiko vines below the village; guests are welcome to join the harvest in August.

highlights.title: Real village life
highlights.detail: Pyrgos is the island's old capital — a hilltop maze of arches and chapels where locals still outnumber visitors.

highlights.title: Aegean views from the roof
highlights.detail: The roof terrace looks over the vineyards to both coasts of the island.

highlights.title: Free parking nearby
highlights.detail: A rare luxury on Santorini — free village lot two minutes' walk away.

stays.description: A 200-year-old village house under the Venetian castle at the top of Pyrgos, restored simply: thick whitewashed walls, arched niches, chestnut shutters, and a roof terrace above the vineyards with the sea on both horizons. This is the Santorini of church bells and grandmothers sweeping doorsteps — the caldera towns are 15 minutes away by car, but you'll be glad to come home to the quiet.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Hannah
reviews.text: The antidote to the caldera crowds. We wandered Pyrgos's alleys at dusk with the swallows, ate at the taverna in the square twice, and drank Yiannis's own wine on the roof. Magical.

reviews.author: Marco
reviews.text: Beautifully restored, dead quiet at night, and half the price of anything with a caldera view. You need a car or the bus, but Pyrgos is the best-located village on the island anyway.

reviews.author: Claire
reviews.text: Yiannis brought us tomatoes and eggs from his garden. Watching the sunset light the whole village from the castle two minutes up the lane — better than Oia, no exaggeration.

images.alt: Terracotta terrace with an open door and sharp shadows
Minimal white and earth-toned walls against a blue sky
Living room corner with gallery wall and plants
White bedroom with a tufted bed frame
Sitting room with a yellow armchair and simple styling

stays.name: Villa Lava — Akrotiri Estate with 12m Pool & Sea Views

host.name: Alexandra
host.presence: A dedicated concierge team handles chefs, boats, and transfers; housekeeping visits daily.

highlights.title: Top 5% of homes
highlights.detail: This home is highly ranked based on ratings, reviews, and reliability.

highlights.title: 12-meter private pool
highlights.detail: One of the largest private pools on the island's south coast.

highlights.title: Sunset over the caldera's quiet side
highlights.detail: Akrotiri faces the sunset across the water — the view toward Oia, not from it.

stays.description: A four-bedroom villa built from island stone and volcanic ash render on the slopes above Akrotiri, with a 12-meter pool, pergola dining for ten, and open sea views toward the caldera's western cliffs. Five minutes from the Bronze Age ruins and the Red Beach, fifteen from the tavernas of the fishing harbor — and blissfully far from the crowds. Daily housekeeping and a concierge team are included.
amenities: Private 12m pool - open May to October

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before July 15. Cancel before August 1 for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Rebecca
reviews.text: Three generations, one villa, zero complaints. The pool kept the kids happy for hours while the adults did wine tastings Alexandra's team arranged. The private chef night was the best meal of the trip.

reviews.author: Omar
reviews.text: Eight of us and it never felt tight. Akrotiri is the right call for a group — quiet, parkable, near the ruins and the lighthouse, and the sunset across the water is stunning.

reviews.author: Laura
reviews.text: Flawless week. Housekeeping daily, concierge on WhatsApp, and the outdoor kitchen got used every night. Worth every euro split eight ways.

images.alt: White villa reflected in its still swimming pool
Whitewashed villa terrace with pool and greenery
Modern white villa and pool at dusk
Sheltered courtyard pool between white walls

stays.name: Black Sand Beach House — 60 Steps from Perissa

host.name: Kostas
host.work: Runs a diving school on Perissa beach
host.presence: The dive shop is two doors down — guests get 20% off intro dives and gear rental.

highlights.title: Steps from the black sand
highlights.detail: Sixty steps from your gate to Perissa's volcanic beach and its beach bars.

highlights.title: Under Mesa Vouno
highlights.detail: The rock of Ancient Thera glows red above the beach at sunset.

highlights.title: Great for beach days
highlights.detail: Outdoor shower, cooler, umbrellas, and snorkel gear included.

stays.description: A relaxed two-bedroom beach house a minute's walk from the black volcanic sand of Perissa, on the island's laid-back east coast. Rinse off in the garden shower, nap under the fig tree, and walk to a dozen tavernas and beach bars along the sand. The hike up Mesa Vouno to Ancient Thera starts ten minutes away — go at sunrise before the heat.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Sam
reviews.text: Beach-flip-flops-taverna-repeat. Exactly what we wanted after two nights of caldera prices. Kostas took us on an intro dive to a volcanic reef — highlight of the trip.

reviews.author: Elodie
reviews.text: Perissa is perfect with children: shallow water, dark sand that doesn't blind you, and gyros everywhere. House was clean and had everything for beach days.

reviews.author: Piotr
reviews.text: Great value and location. Wifi struggled on the patio, fine indoors. Would stay again.

reviews.author: Maya
reviews.text: The sunrise hike to Ancient Thera from the house is unmissable. Loved the quiet east-coast pace.

images.alt: Palm-shaded pool with wooden loungers
Quiet beach shoreline at golden hour
Sun umbrellas and palms along a sandy beach
Cozy living room with plants and a linen sofa

stays.name: Ammoudi Cliff Suite — Cave Rooms Above the Red Bay
stays.typeLabel: Entire rental unit in Oia, Greece

host.name: Margarita
host.work: Family fish taverna at Ammoudi Bay
host.presence: Our family taverna sits on the water below — mention you're our guest and the day's catch is on the house terrace by eight.

highlights.title: Above Amoudi Bay
highlights.detail: The 214 red-rock steps to the island's best seafood harbor start at your door.

highlights.title: Swim from the rocks
highlights.detail: Five minutes down to the swimming rocks and cliff-jump point opposite Agios Nikolaos islet.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the keypad.

stays.description: A cave suite burrowed into the red cliff on Oia's western edge, directly above the fishing harbor of Amoudi. Fall asleep to halyards clinking below and wake to fishermen unloading the morning catch. The vaulted bedroom and skylit bath are carved into the rock; the terrace hangs over the bay with the sunset dead ahead. Down the famous steps: four fish tavernas and the clearest swimming water on the island.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before July 22. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Freya
reviews.text: Swimming at Amoudi before breakfast, grilled octopus at the family taverna for dinner, sunset from our own terrace in between. The steps back up are the price of paradise and worth every one.

reviews.author: Andrés
reviews.text: The cave rooms are gorgeously done — cool, quiet, that skylight shower. Margarita's taverna treated us like family all week.

reviews.author: Jess
reviews.text: Most romantic place we've ever stayed. Watch the boats come in with a glass of Vinsanto and you'll never want to leave.

images.alt: Amoudi Bay's red cliffs and fishing boats below Oia
Cave hotel terraces and a curved pool above the sea
Blue-domed chapel framed by pink bougainvillea

stays.name: Canava Estate Megalochori — Winery Grounds & Pool

host.name: The Argyros Family
host.presence: The estate is a working vineyard — join our cellar tasting any evening at six, guests taste free.

highlights.title: Stay on a working vineyard
highlights.detail: A converted 19th-century canava (wine cellar house) amid basket-pruned Assyrtiko vines.

highlights.title: Evening tastings included
highlights.detail: Daily estate wine tastings in the old cellar are free for guests.

highlights.title: Newly opened
highlights.detail: Converted and opened to guests in 2025.

stays.description: The estate's 19th-century canava — the vaulted cellar house where the family pressed wine for a century — converted into a three-bedroom villa amid the vineyards outside Megalochori. Stone vaults, chestnut doors, a pool between the vines, and the smell of fermenting Assyrtiko in September. Megalochori's bell-towered square is a five-minute walk; the caldera rim at sunset, ten by car.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before July 20. Cancel before August 5 for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Charlotte
reviews.text: Tastings in the cellar where the wine was actually made, dinners under the pergola, mornings in the pool looking at vines. Megalochori is the prettiest village nobody visits.

reviews.author: Nikolai
reviews.text: The vaulted ceilings are spectacular and the estate wines are seriously good — we shipped a case home. A completely different Santorini.

reviews.author: Aoife
reviews.text: Beautiful, calm, spacious. You'll want a car for beaches and the caldera, but that's the trade for the quiet.

images.alt: White cubic villa with a private pool
Ripe grapes on the vine in late sun
Rooftop terrace at sunset over rolling hills

experiences.name: Caldera sunset sail on a luxury catamaran

host.name: Captain Vangelis
host.bio: Santorini-born skipper with twenty years sailing the caldera. Runs a small fleet of catamarans out of Vlychada with his brothers, all licensed captains.

experiences.description: Sail the caldera's full arc — Red Beach, White Beach, the hot springs at the volcano, and swim stops in water 300 meters deep. The crew grills a full Greek BBQ on board with local wine, and you drift below Oia's cliffs just as the sun drops. Unlimited drinks, snorkel gear, and hotel transfers included.

images.alt: Sailboat silhouetted against a peach sunset at sea
Catamaran under sail as the sun sets
On deck of a catamaran heading out to open water

experiences.name: Akrotiri ruins & Red Beach with an archaeologist

host.name: Dr. Ioanna
host.bio: Field archaeologist who excavated at Akrotiri for six seasons. PhD on Cycladic Bronze Age trade; guides small groups when not digging.

experiences.description: Walk the covered excavation of Akrotiri — the 'Pompeii of the Aegean,' a Minoan-era town frozen by the volcanic eruption 3,600 years ago — with an archaeologist who worked the site. Three-story houses, drainage systems, and the ghost imprints of wooden beds. Finish on the red volcanic cliffs of Red Beach as Ioanna reconstructs the eruption that made the caldera.

images.alt: Columns of an ancient Greek ruin under a dramatic sky
Weathered marble of an ancient Greek temple
Volcanic cliffs meeting deep blue water near Akrotiri

experiences.name: Volcanic vineyard tasting at a Pyrgos winery

host.name: Petros
host.bio: Sommelier and son of a Pyrgos grape-growing family. Studied oenology in Athens and Bordeaux before coming home to the family's basket-pruned vines.

experiences.description: Taste eight wines on a terrace above the caldera slope — bone-dry Assyrtiko, barrel-aged Nykteri, and sun-dried Vinsanto — while Petros explains how vines survive on volcanic ash with no rain, coiled into ground-hugging baskets against the meltemi wind. Includes a walk through 150-year-old ungrafted vineyards and a cellar visit, with local cheese and tomato paximadia between pours.

images.alt: Glass of wine overlooking vineyard rows
Stainless steel tanks inside a modern winery
Friends toasting with glasses of red wine

experiences.name: Santorinian cooking class: fava, tomatokeftedes & white eggplant

host.name: Kyria Anna
host.bio: Retired school cook who has fed three generations of Exo Gonia. Grows her own capers, cherry tomatoes, and white eggplant on terraces behind the house.

experiences.description: Cook the island's PDO ingredients in Anna's farmhouse kitchen: silky Santorini fava with caramelized onions, crisp tomatokeftedes from her own waterless cherry tomatoes, white eggplant baked with kopanisti, and melitinia pastries for dessert. Everything is eaten under the vine pergola with wine from the neighbor's canava. You'll leave with her handwritten recipes.

images.alt: Cook folding a bowl of ripe tomatoes and herbs
Tomato and feta salad plated in dappled sunlight
Well-worn wooden spoons on a rustic table

experiences.name: Fira to Oia caldera-rim hike at golden hour

host.name: Thanos
host.bio: Mountain guide and geology teacher raised in Fira. Has walked the rim path over a thousand times and still stops for the view at Skaros.

experiences.description: The classic 10-kilometer walk along the caldera's edge from Fira through Firostefani and Imerovigli to Oia — past Skaros Rock, the chapel of Profitis Ilias, and long empty stretches where the only sound is wind and church bells. Thanos times the walk so you crest the final ridge into Oia as the sunset begins. Water, trail snacks, and a celebratory drink in Oia included.

images.alt: White village clinging to the caldera cliffs
Aerial view of the cliff path past terraced white suites
Hiker walking a rugged trail with mountains ahead

experiences.name: Oia golden-hour photography walk

host.name: Lena
host.bio: Travel photographer based on Santorini for nine years; shoots for Greek tourism campaigns and knows every unmarked rooftop and quiet dome in Oia.

experiences.description: Skip the tripod queues. Lena leads you through Oia's back lanes to the angles the crowds never find — hidden dome clusters, marble lanes lit gold, and rooftops where the caldera unrolls beneath you. Hands-on help with composition and light for phone or camera, timed to end at a private sunset spot away from the castle crush. Includes 10 edited portraits of you against the view.

images.alt: Camera body and lenses laid out on a dark surface
Traveler seated on a white rooftop ledge above the caldera
Blue-domed churches stacked above the deep blue sea in Oia

experiences.name: Sea kayaking the south coast caves and lighthouse

host.name: Alex
host.bio: Sea-kayak instructor and marine-life nerd who paddled the entire Cyclades over three summers before settling under the Akrotiri lighthouse.

experiences.description: Paddle stable tandem kayaks beneath the layered lava cliffs of the south coast — through sea caves, past the White and Red beaches unreachable by road, to a snorkel stop in a hidden cove below the Akrotiri lighthouse. Calm morning water, a light picnic of local cheese and fruit on a pebble beach, and dry bags, gear, and photos included.

images.alt: Aerial view of a boat moored off a pale sandy cove
Clear shallow water rippling over pale sand
Calm shoreline at golden hour

experiences.name: Freediving & snorkeling at Amoudi Bay

host.name: Nefeli
host.bio: AIDA-certified freediving instructor and former competitive swimmer. Teaches breath-hold in the deep clear water below Oia every summer.

experiences.description: Amoudi's water drops away fast and impossibly clear — perfect for a first taste of freediving. Nefeli covers breathing and relaxation on the swimming rocks, then guides you down the anchor line in stages, with snorkel circuits around Agios Nikolaos islet between sessions. Wetsuits, masks, and fins provided; finish with fresh juice at the harbor tavernas.

images.alt: Looking up through deep blue water toward the light
Diver surrounded by a school of fish
Amoudi Bay's red cliffs and clear harbor water

experiences.name: Volcano & hot springs cruise to Nea Kameni

host.name: Captain Mihalis
host.bio: Third-generation boatman whose grandfather ferried geologists to the 1950 eruption. Sails a traditional wooden kaiki from the old port.

experiences.description: Cross the caldera by wooden kaiki to Nea Kameni, the black lava island still steaming at its crater rims, and hike the 30-minute cinder path to the summit vents with views back at the whole cliff line. Then anchor at Palea Kameni's iron-red hot springs for a warm swim before the sail home beneath Fira. A proper island classic — bring sturdy shoes and a dark swimsuit.

images.alt: Catamarans and boats moored in a quiet anchorage
Sailboat crossing calm water at sunset
Yachts anchored in a caldera cove beneath the cliffs

experiences.name: Hidden villages walk: Pyrgos, Megalochori & Emporio

host.name: Sofia
host.bio: Folklorist and lifelong Emporio resident who wrote her thesis on the island's fortified settlements. Her grandmother's house anchors the walk's coffee stop.

experiences.description: Inland Santorini, where the tour buses don't fit: the Venetian kasteli of Pyrgos, Megalochori's bell towers and hidden canavas, and the astonishing goulas fortress maze of Emporio, whose arched lanes were built to confuse pirates. Greek coffee and melitinia in Sofia's family courtyard, stories of weddings and sieges, and not a single caldera crowd in sight.

images.alt: Whitewashed lane with a blue gate and flowering wall
Church bell towers against a clear blue sky
Hand-painted taverna sign on an ochre village wall

services.name: Anemos — cliffside dining above Skaros

host.name: Chef Andreas
host.bio: Ex-Athens fine dining, returned to the island to cook his grandmother's recipes with technique. Every table on the terrace faces Skaros Rock.

services.description: Terraced into the Imerovigli cliff with every table facing the caldera, Anemos plates modern Greek built on island produce — fava with smoked eel, lamb with santorini capers, and a deconstructed tomatokeftedes that regulars order twice. Book the 19:30 seating for sunset over Skaros; the wine list runs deep on old-vine Assyrtiko.

images.alt: Terrace restaurant tables overlooking the water
Greek salad and a glass of rosé on a taverna table
Shaded terrace table and chairs facing the caldera

services.name: Taverna Katina — fish tavern on Amoudi Bay

host.name: The Pagoni Family
host.bio: Three generations grilling the morning catch at the water's edge of Amoudi since 1972. The octopus dries on lines beside the tables, as it always has.

services.description: Tables on the quay so close to the water that spray reaches your feet on a windy day. Pick your fish from the ice — red mullet, sea bream, lobster for the spaghetti — and start with sun-dried octopus off the charcoal and white taramosalata. Come down the steps before sunset, eat as the light goes red on the cliff, and let them call you a donkey taxi for the climb back.

images.alt: Octopus drying on a line by the water in the sun
Taverna tables under a tree at the water's edge
Seaside taverna tables on a whitewashed terrace

services.name: Canava Roussos cellar tastings

host.name: Markos
host.bio: Cellar master of a family winery pressing Santorini grapes since 1836. Pours vertical Vinsanto flights in the original vaulted canava.

services.description: One of the island's oldest working wineries, still centered on its 19th-century vaulted cellar dug into the ash. Flights move from steel-fresh Assyrtiko through oak-aged Nykteri to Vinsanto aged twelve years in old barrels — sunset-orange, honeyed, unforgettable. Tastings come with island cheeses and chlorotyri, and the courtyard under the pistachio tree is the place to lose an afternoon.

images.alt: Wine bottles lining a cellar shelf
Hands cradling freshly harvested dark grapes
Grapes ripening on the vine in late sun

services.name: To Fournaki — bakery & loukoumades in Fira

host.name: Kyria Despina
host.bio: Has fired the wood oven behind the bus square every morning at 4 a.m. for thirty years. Her loukoumades recipe came from her mother in Anafi.

services.description: Follow the smell of wood smoke off Fira's main square. Despina's counter sells sesame-crusted village bread, spanakopita in crackling phyllo, and melitinia — the island's Easter cheese tarts — year-round. The move: a paper cone of loukoumades straight from the fryer, drowned in thyme honey and cinnamon, eaten standing on the church steps opposite. Espresso freddo from the grandson's machine completes it.

images.alt: Bakery case filled with fresh breads and pastries
Rustic loaves dusted with flour
Blue-shuttered cafe front with a wooden barrel table

services.name: Petra & Thalassa — tasting menus over Oia

host.name: Chef Elias
host.bio: Two stints in Copenhagen kitchens before coming home to cook the Aegean: caper leaves, saffron from Krokos, and fish landed at Ammoudi that morning.

services.description: Nine courses in a candlelit cave dining room carved beneath Oia's marble lane — smoked fava with sea urchin, white eggplant three ways, monkfish in Vinsanto beurre blanc. The wine pairing leans local and rare, including single-vineyard Assyrtiko you won't find exported. Two seatings; the later one ends with petit fours on a terrace over the dark caldera.

images.alt: Server presenting a finely plated tasting course
Intimate restaurant dining room with warm lighting
Vividly plated bowl of fresh vegetables and grains

services.name: Private chef Ariadne — villa dinners & BBQ

host.name: Ariadne
host.bio: Cooked in Mykonos and Athens hotels before going solo; now cooks in villas across the island with a basket of whatever her father's garden gave her that morning.

services.description: Ariadne arrives with coolers, sets your villa table with linen and candles, and cooks a five-course Santorinian menu while you swim — fava tartlets, grilled sea bass with ladolemono, slow lamb with island herbs, and a semolina orange cake her yiayia would recognize. BBQ, meze-only, and vegetarian menus available; she shops the Pyrgos farmers' market and names every grower at the table.

images.alt: Chefs preparing dinner together in a modern kitchen
Fresh vegetables and eggs laid out on a prep board
Colorful bowls of seasonal vegetables ready to serve

services.name: Tsipouro & Co — sunset wine bar in Fira

host.name: Stelios
host.bio: Sommelier who worked London wine bars for a decade, came home, and opened forty Greek wines by the glass on a caldera-facing balcony.

services.description: A narrow balcony bar hanging off Fira's caldera walkway with the best-value sunset seat in town — no minimum spend, just good glasses. Forty Greek wines by the glass, tsipouro and mastiha flights, and small plates built to keep pace: smoked mackerel on paximadi, grilled talagani, capers fried crisp. Arrive 45 minutes before sundown for a rail seat.

images.alt: Backlit bar lined with bottles at night
Bartender straining a drink into a glass
Glasses of red wine raised in a toast

services.name: I Plateia — family taverna on Pyrgos square

host.name: The Karamolegos Family
host.bio: Mother in the kitchen, father at the grill, daughters on the floor. The menu is whatever the garden and the butcher provided that day, chalked on a board.

services.description: Tables scattered under the plane tree on Pyrgos's little square, paper tablecloths pinned against the breeze. Order the chalkboard: fava churned with onions, white eggplant off the grill, rabbit stifado, and tomatokeftedes that set the island standard. The house wine comes from the uncle's canava down the lane and the bill will make you double-check it. No bookings — come early or wait with a tsipouro.

images.alt: Pastel courtyard taverna beneath flowering wisteria
Turquoise taverna storefront with a barrel table
Greek salad with bread and olives on a taverna table

services.name: Mavro Ammos — beach taverna on Perivolos sand

host.name: Giorgos
host.bio: Started as a beach-bar boy on this stretch of black sand at sixteen; now runs the kitchen, the loungers, and the best grilled calamari on the south coast.

services.description: Barefoot lunch on the black sand of Perivolos: tables at the water line, mezze arriving in waves — grilled calamari, sardines in vine leaves, watermelon with feta — and a cold Assyrtiko sweating in the bucket. Loungers and umbrellas are free with a kitchen order, the swim between courses is mandatory, and afternoons dissolve into DJ sets as the light goes gold.

images.alt: Spread of mezze dishes across a shared table
Courtyard taverna tables beneath a canvas awning
Sun umbrellas and palms along a sandy beach

services.name: Aegean Frames — portrait photographer in Oia

host.name: Dimitra
host.bio: Wedding and portrait photographer with twelve seasons on the caldera. Shoots film and digital; her proposal shots have gone viral more than once.

services.description: Sunrise or blue-hour portrait sessions through Oia's lanes and rooftops — engagements, honeymoons, families, or a solo shoot against the domes. Dimitra scouts quiet corners the day before, moves fast between spots before the crowds build, and delivers 60 edited images within 72 hours. Flowing-dress rental and a champagne finish on a private rooftop available as add-ons.

images.alt: Vintage camera with printed photographs and a map
Portrait subject seated on a rooftop above the caldera
Oia's iconic blue domes above the Aegean
